about.title: Fresno Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription:
Public records show 53 people died on Fresno roads in 2025, and behind each of those numbers is a family trying to figure out what comes next. Some of those losses happened along SR-41 or SR-99; others on Blackstone Avenue or Shaw Avenue, streets most people drive without a second thought. Wrongful death cases in Fresno County are not limited to traffic. A fall on unsafe property, a medical error, or a workplace incident can also give rise to a claim.

California law lets a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children bring the case first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The claim is civil and moves separately from any criminal charges, so a family does not have to wait for a prosecutor's decision. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance.

LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Fresno families with an independent attorney who reviews the situation and, if there is a case, works on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits who has standing: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you are connected with sorts this out early so the right people are named from the start.

items.title: The two-year deadline stays in view
items.desc: A wrongful death action in California generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting connected sooner protects that time.

items.title: Every category of loss is considered
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, the income and support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their companionship and guidance are all recoverable under California law. Your attorney builds the claim around your family's actual losses, and you owe no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The driver who caused my father's crash on SR-99 in Fresno is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from anything the Fresno County District Attorney does. Your family can move forward regardless of whether charges are filed or how the criminal case turns out. Waiting can actually work against you, since the two-year civil deadline keeps running.

items.question: My sister was unmarried and had no children. Can her parents or siblings file a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Possibly. When there is no surviving spouse, domestic partner, or child, California allows certain other heirs and people who were financially dependent on the person to bring the claim. Who qualifies depends on the family's specific circumstances, which is exactly what an attorney will look at during a free review.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect us with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service and not a law firm. The independent attorney we connect you with works on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless your family receives a recovery. You can ask about the specifics of that arrangement before deciding anything.
